title: Global military spending rise continues as European and Asian expenditures surge
date_evidence: (Stockholm, 27 April 2026) World military expenditure reached $2887 billion in 2025, an increase of 2.9 per cent in real terms over 2024.
key_claim: European military spending rose 14 per cent to $864 billion in 2025, the sharpest growth in Central and Western Europe since the cold war; US spending fell 7.5 per cent to $954 billion; 22 of 29 European NATO members spent at least 2 per cent of GDP.
frame_summary: Europe is rearming faster than at any time since the early cold war precisely as the United States pulls back its own spending, marking a structural shift toward European self-reliance.
verbatim_quote: the main contributor to the global increase in military spending in 2025 was a 14 per cent rise in Europe to $864 billion

title: EDIP | Forging Europe's Defence
date_evidence: General publications 30 March 2026 EDIP Regulation; General publications 30 March 2026 EDIP - Financing decision and work programme
key_claim: The EUR 1.5 billion EDIP programme funds Industrial Reinforcement Actions of over EUR 700 million; the first Member State reinforcement call had a submission deadline of 16 June 2026 and Common Procurement calls close in October 2026 and February 2027.
frame_summary: The EU now has a funded, calendared industrial programme to ramp up defence production capacity, but its first grants and deliveries are only beginning to move through the pipeline.
verbatim_quote: With over EUR 700 million of funding, IRA is EDIPs largest component and aims to ramp-up defence production in Europe and Ukraine.

title: Hegseth Launches Review of US Military Presence in Europe, Taking Aim at 'Free-Riding' NATO Allies
key_claim: On 18 June 2026 Defense Secretary Hegseth told NATO the US is launching a six-month review of its European posture, confirmed the NATO Force Model cuts are 'immediate', and warned US dues to NATO's budget will fall where allies underspend.
frame_summary: Washington is deliberately and quickly reducing its conventional commitment to European defence and tying continued support to allied spending, forcing Europe to backfill capabilities it does not yet have.
verbatim_quote: The U.S. is lowering its contribution, still considerable, but somewhat lower than it was in the past. What you see there is that the Europeans are now backfilling it.

title: What Defense Leaders Will Discuss At The 2026 NATO Summit
key_claim: Defence ministers and leaders gather in Ankara on 7-8 July 2026 for a summit centred on turning the 2025 Hague 5 per cent pledge into production, procurement and burden-sharing, against the Russia-Ukraine war backdrop.
frame_summary: The Ankara summit is where the alliance's 5 per cent spending pledge is meant to convert from headline commitment into concrete production and procurement, keeping rearmament momentum in the foreground.

title: At a NATO range in Latvia, hits and misses mark Europe's counter-drone journey
key_claim: European counter-drone startups demonstrated interceptors at NATO's new Selija uncrewed-systems range after Latvia proved unable to challenge repeated drone incursions, and is deploying mobile interceptor teams to its Russian border.
frame_summary: Europe's eastern flank is under sustained drone incursion pressure and its counter-drone response, while accelerating through NATO ranges and mobile teams, is still catching up to a threat a couple of steps ahead.
verbatim_quote: countries on its eastern flank have found themselves unable to fend off multiple drone incursions in recent months

title: NATO AIRCOM Industry Day advances counter-drone innovation for Eastern Sentry
key_claim: AIRCOM Industry Day on 30 June and 1 July 2026 gathered 34 companies from more than 20 countries on counter-uncrewed systems for Eastern Sentry, with NATO's Layered Counter-UAS Initiative eXperimental accelerating fielding.
frame_summary: NATO is institutionalising counter-drone defence of its eastern flank into a standing multi-domain air-defence posture, moving it from ad hoc response toward an established programme.
verbatim_quote: The event brought together representatives from 34 hi-tech companies and participants from more than 20 countries

title: How Ukraine's Drone Innovation Reversed Russia's Momentum
key_claim: Ukraine produced an estimated four million robotic and autonomous systems in 2025 and is on track for five to six million in 2026; drones now generate 75-85 per cent of frontline casualties, and its defence industrial base iterates from prototype to frontline in weeks.
frame_summary: Ukraine's combat-proven, fast-iterating drone industrial base is the most advanced in Europe and is becoming a scalable asset that European partners can plug into.
signals_supported: Ukrainian drone innovation scaling into Europe
verbatim_quote: Ukraine was able to produce an estimated four million robotic and autonomous systems in 2025, and is, by all counts, on track to produce between five million to six million in 2026

title: A Defense Production Plan for Europe
date_evidence: <meta property="article:published_time" content="2026-05-20T17:25:12+00:00"> By Luka Ignac May 20, 2026
key_claim: Europe's production shortages cluster in air-defence interceptors, precision-guided munitions and artillery rockets; without industrial capacity, new budgets default to off-the-shelf US platforms, with about 51 per cent of European NATO equipment spending in 2022-2024 going to the US.
frame_summary: Money alone will not deliver European deterrence; without a deliberate plan to build the allied industrial base, higher budgets deepen dependence on delayed US supply.
verbatim_quote: The continent's production shortages cluster in exactly the categories the war exposed: air defense interceptors, precision-guided munitions, and artillery rockets.

title: Seabed zero: Baltic sabotage and the global risks to undersea infrastructure
key_claim: Western economies depend on data and energy flow along the seafloor, and Russia and China are weaponising that dependency through repeated Baltic cable and pipeline incidents, exposing limited legal authority to act in international waters.
frame_summary: Undersea cables and pipelines are a growing grey-zone target that Europe is only beginning to defend, with the threat outpacing the legal and physical tools available.
verbatim_quote: Western economies have become dependent on data and energy flow along the seafloor; Russia and China are weaponizing that dependency.

title: The Critical Entities Resilience Directive: Compliance Readiness Before and After July 2026
date_evidence: Standing advisory page marked 'Updated'; anchors the binding 17 July 2026 CER designation deadline, a matter of public EU law rather than the article date
key_claim: By 17 July 2026 EU member states must identify and notify critical entities under the CER Directive across 11 sectors, after which each entity has a compressed roughly ten-month window to meet all-hazards resilience obligations covering sabotage and hybrid threats.
frame_summary: The EU is hard-wiring resilience against sabotage and hybrid threats into binding obligations for critical operators, with the July 2026 designation milestone forcing the issue onto boards.
signals_supported: Hybrid threats, sabotage and resilience rules
verbatim_quote: By 17 July 2026, EU Member States are required to have identified which organizations on their territory qualify as “critical entities” under the Directive.
